hints: When multiplying complex numbers in exponential form, multiply their moduli and add their arguments.
Apply this separately to $\omega z_1$ and $\omega z_2$, using the factor $2$ and angle $\pi/2$ from $\omega$.
Check that each resulting argument lies in $-\pi<\theta\le\pi$; adjust by $2\pi$ only if necessary.
walkthrough:
Multiply moduli and add arguments to calculate $\omega z_1$:
$$\omega z_1 = \left(2\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{2}\mathrm{i}}\right)\left(3\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{4}\mathrm{i}}\right)$$
$$r_1 = 2 \times 3 = 6$$
$$\theta_1 = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{2\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$$
$$\text{Since } -\pi < \dfrac{3\pi}{4} \leqslant \pi: \quad \omega z_1 = 6\mathrm{e}^{\frac{3\pi}{4}\mathrm{i}}$$

Multiply moduli and add arguments to calculate $\omega z_2$:
$$\omega z_2 = \left(2\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{2}\mathrm{i}}\right)\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{6}\mathrm{i}}\right)$$
$$r_2 = 2 \times \dfrac{3}{2} = 3$$
$$\theta_2 = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{3\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{4\pi}{6} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$$
$$\text{Since } -\pi < \dfrac{2\pi}{3} \leqslant \pi: \quad \omega z_2 = 3\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi}{3}\mathrm{i}}$$

hints: A number $re^{i\theta}$ is plotted at distance $r$ from the origin and angle $\theta$ measured anticlockwise from the positive real axis.
Plot $A$ with modulus $3$ and argument $\pi/4$, and $B$ with modulus $3/2$ and argument $\pi/6$.
Use the products from part (a) to plot $C$ and $D$: each ray is rotated by $\pi/2$ and each distance from $O$ is doubled.
walkthrough:
Identify the modulus and argument for points $A$ and $B$ in the first quadrant:
$$A \; (z_1): \quad r = 3, \quad \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4} = 45^{\circ}$$
$$B \; (z_2): \quad r = \dfrac{3}{2} = 1.5, \quad \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6} = 30^{\circ}$$
$$\text{Plot } A \text{ and } B \text{ in the first quadrant with } B \text{ closer to the origin and at a lower angle than } A.$$

Identify the modulus and argument for points $C$ and $D$ in the second quadrant:
$$C \; (\omega z_1): \quad r = 6, \quad \theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4} = 135^{\circ}$$
$$D \; (\omega z_2): \quad r = 3, \quad \theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3} = 120^{\circ}$$
$$\text{Plot } C \text{ and } D \text{ in the second quadrant such that } OC \text{ has twice the length of } OA \text{ and is perpendicular to } OA,$$
$$\text{and } OD \text{ has twice the length of } OB \text{ and is perpendicular to } OB.$$

hints: In multiplication by $re^{i\theta}$, the modulus $r$ gives the scale factor and the argument $\theta$ gives the rotation about the origin.
Read these two quantities directly from $\omega=2e^{\pi i/2}$.
State the rotation direction as well as its angle, and state the enlargement scale factor.
walkthrough:
Analyze the effect of the argument of the multiplier $\omega = 2\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{2}\mathrm{i}}$:
$$\arg(\omega) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \implies \text{adds } \dfrac{\pi}{2} \text{ radians to the argument of each complex number.}$$
$$\text{Geometric effect 1: A rotation of } \dfrac{\pi}{2} \text{ radians (or } 90^{\circ}\text{) anticlockwise about the origin } O.$$

Analyze the effect of the modulus of the multiplier $\omega = 2\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{2}\mathrm{i}}$:
$$|\omega| = 2 \implies \text{multiplies the distance of each point from the origin by } 2.$$
$$\text{Geometric effect 2: An enlargement of scale factor } 2 \text{ with centre at the origin } O.$$
